fix: restore Android autolinking and runtime on RN 0.84 + new arch

The 5.0.0-alpha.2/3 releases shipped broken on Android: the native
module was not autolinked, and once linked the example app crashed in
release builds. This bundles all the necessary fixes so the example
APK builds and runs end-to-end on the new architecture.

react-native.config (rename `.js` → `.cjs`):
  package.json has `"type": "module"`, so Node treats `.js` files as
  ESM. The CLI loads dependency configs via `cosmiconfigSync` (uses
  `require()`), which cannot load ESM — on Node 18/20 it throws
  ERR_REQUIRE_ESM and the loader silently falls back to an empty
  config; on Node 22+ it returns `{ __esModule, default }` whose shape
  fails schema validation. Either way RNViewShotPackage was never
  registered. Forcing CJS via `.cjs` fixes loading on every Node.

package.json `"react-native"` field:
  Was set to a Windows platform config object — Metro silently fell
  back to `"main": "lib/index.js"` (compiled output). Set it to
  `"src/index.tsx"` so Metro bundles the source. The Windows config
  already lives in `react-native.config.cjs` where it belongs.

example/metro.config.js — duplicate React/RN guard:
  Metro resolved `react`/`react-native` from the lib's own
  `node_modules` (lib's devDependency) AND the example's, bundling
  both. With React 19, `useRef` is inlined as
  `ReactSharedInternals.H.useRef(...)` — only one copy has its
  dispatcher set by the renderer, so hooks called through the other
  crashed with `Cannot read property 'useRef' of null` (inside RN
  core's `View_withRef`, the first forwardRef component rendered
  under <ViewShot>). Block the parent `node_modules/{react,
  react-native}` and drop `../node_modules` from `nodeModulesPaths`,
  mirroring the working `example-expo/metro.config.js`.

src/index.tsx — class → functional + ref shape preserved:
  Class components could trigger lazy `View` loading on the
  `mqt_v_native` thread under new arch, where TurboModuleRegistry
  cannot reach `PlatformConstants`. Convert to a functional component
  with `forwardRef` so render happens on the JS thread.
  Backward-compat for the v4 ref API: `viewShotRef.current` is the
  inner `<View>` (so `findNodeHandle(ref.current)` keeps working),
  with `capture()` attached as a property on that node so
  `viewShotRef.current.capture()` still works. `ViewShotRef` is now
  `View & { capture: () => Promise<string> }`.

CI build-apk.yml:
  Build the example APK with `-PnewArchEnabled=true`. The example's
  `gradle.properties` keeps `newArchEnabled=false` for Detox E2E
  compatibility (Fabric crashes on the emulator there); the CI APK
  needs new arch so TurboModuleRegistry resolves RNViewShot and
  PlatformConstants.

src/specs/NativeRNViewShot.ts:
  Drop unused `Platform` import.

fix(android): snapshotContentContainer captures off-screen content

When snapshotContentContainer:true is used on a ScrollView, Android
used to draw the scrollview at its expanded canvas size but the
children below the visible viewport were skipped because of the
scrollview's own clipping. iOS gets this right by temporarily
resizing the scrollview to its content size before drawing. Mirror
that behaviour: inside the existing UIManager-queue runnable, save
layout params + scroll position, force an exact measure/layout at
content height, draw, then restore — so the live UI never observes a
half-applied state. Width/height reads and bitmap allocation also
move inside the UI runnable so two concurrent captures of the same
view can't race on the transiently-expanded geometry.

When snapshotContentContainer is requested on a non-ScrollView ref
the unconditional cast is replaced with a fallback (warn + capture
visible bounds) instead of throwing ClassCastException.

README updated to call out that Android's expansion is vertical-only
(HorizontalScrollView isn't widened) and that FlatList virtualization
can still skip off-screen items at the React layer regardless.

Adds JUnit/Mockito coverage for the forceExactLayout helper.

fix(types): support React Native 0.87 Strict TypeScript API

RN 0.87 makes the Strict TypeScript API the default, which breaks two
type-level assumptions in this package:

- `react-native/Libraries/*` subpaths now resolve to `types: null`, so the
  deep `CodegenTypes` import has no types. RN re-exports the same types as a
  `CodegenTypes` namespace from the package root; `WithDefault<number, -1>`
  resolves identically, so codegen output is unchanged.
- `View` is a function component, not a class, so it is no longer usable as
  a ref instance type. `React.ComponentRef<typeof View>` resolves to the
  instance type under both the legacy and strict typings.

Verified with `tsc --noEmit` against react-native 0.87.1 in an app that uses
both `captureRef` and `<ViewShot>`.
